title: National Burden of Human Adenovirus Infections in China: A Community-Based Multiplier Modeling Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human adenovirus (HAdV) is an important cause of respiratory infections, yet community-level burden estimates remain limited. The study aimed to estimate post-pandemic HAdV burden in China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Using nationwide respiratory pathogen surveillance data and a multiplier model, the study estimated the incidence of HAdV infections, symptomatic illnesses (SI), and medically attended illnesses (MAI) in China from 2023 to 2024.
analysis.methods: Age-, species-, and province-specific analyses were conducted, and uncertainty was assessed using Monte Carlo simulations.
analysis.main_results: We estimated 44.21 million HAdV infections (95% UI, 26.68–77.08 million) over the 19-month study period, corresponding to an average monthly incidence of 1.58 per 1000 persons (95% UI, 1.01–2.61). The estimated average monthly incidences of SI and MAI were 0.41 (95% UI, 0.30–0.57) and 0.30 (95% UI, 0.21–0.40) per 1000 persons, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HAdV imposed a substantial and under-recognized respiratory disease burden in China during the post-pandemic period, with children aged 0–4 years experiencing the highest burden and marked species-specific and geographic heterogeneity observed.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide community-based evidence to inform adenovirus surveillance and respiratory disease control strategies in China.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study highlights that children experienced the highest burden and marked species-specific and geographic heterogeneity were observed, which may limit generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on modeling and surveillance data.

analysis.summary_en: This study estimated the national burden of human adenovirus (HAdV) infections in China from 2023 to 2024 using a multiplier model with nationwide surveillance data. The findings revealed 44.21 million HAdV infections over 19 months, with an average monthly incidence of 1.58 per 1000 persons. Children aged 0–4 years had the highest incidence (16.66 per 1000 persons), and significant geographic variation was observed, with higher rates in south-central and southwestern provinces. The study also noted substantial burden of symptomatic and medically attended illnesses, emphasizing the need for enhanced surveillance and targeted control strategies. The evidence strength is moderate, limited by modeling assumptions and geographic heterogeneity.

title: Development and analytical evaluation of a microneutralization cytopathic effect assay for human adenovirus type 55-specific neutralizing antibodies

analysis.research_question_and_background: Reliable quantification of neutralizing antibodies (nAb) against human adenovirus type 55 (HAdV-55) is critical for the evaluation of emerging vaccine candidates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study established and analytically validated a microneutralization assay based on cytopathic effect (MN-CPE) as a scalable alternative for HAdV-55-specific nAb quantification.
analysis.methods: Comparative performance analysis was conducted between the MN-CPE assay and the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT), assessing dilution linearity, relative accuracy using high-, middle-, and low-titer reference sera, and negative-control acceptance ranges.
analysis.main_results: Both assays maintained high dilution linearity, with coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.988 for MN-CPE and 0.9926 for PRNT, and demonstrated acceptable responses across the dynamic range. The MN-CPE assay provided a distinct statistical advantage over PRNT by defining a negative-control acceptance range.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the MN-CPE assay is analytically comparable to PRNT and serves as a practical, relatively high-capacity alternative for HAdV-55 neutralization testing in clinical and preclinical vaccine research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a scalable and efficient method for quantifying HAdV-55-specific neutralizing antibodies, which is essential for evaluating vaccine candidates and advancing clinical and preclinical research.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study demonstrates high analytical comparability between MN-CPE and PRNT, with evidence strength supported by rigorous validation and testing across multiple parameters, though limitations related to generalizability beyond HAdV-55 were not explicitly addressed.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed and validated a microneutralization cytopathic effect assay (MN-CPE) as an alternative to the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) for quantifying neutralizing antibodies against human adenovirus type 55 (HAdV-55). The MN-CPE assay demonstrated high dilution linearity (R2 = 0.988) and comparable performance to PRNT (R2 = 0.9926), with the added advantage of defining a negative-control acceptance range. Both assays successfully detected HAdV-55-specific nAbs in immunized cynomolgus macaques without cross-reactivity to other HAdV types. The MN-CPE assay offers a practical, high-capacity alternative for HAdV-55 neutralization testing in clinical and preclinical vaccine research.

title: Identification of Human Adenovirus Species in Stool Sample from Children with Diarrhea in Najaf Governorate Using Species-Specific Hexon Gene PCR Assays.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify the prevalence of human adenovirus species in stool samples from children with diarrhea in Najaf Governorate, as human adenoviruses are recognized as significant viral pathogens associated with a wide range of clinical manifestations, including acute gastroenteritis, particularly among pediatric populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted between March and July 2025, collecting stool samples from children presenting with acute diarrhea at hospitals in Najaf Governorate. A total of 100 stool samples were analyzed.
analysis.methods: The samples were analyzed using multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for the detection of adenovirus species A–F, with species-specific Hexon gene PCR assays employed to identify the specific adenovirus species present.
analysis.main_results: Adenovirus species F was the most frequently detected species (29%), followed by species C (15.9%), D (13.6%), E (11.3%), and B (6.8%) and A (6.8%). Co-detection of adenovirus species F and B was observed in 13.6% of samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings confirm the dominant etiological role of adenovirus species F in diarrheal disease, while also highlighting the presence of other species, which may have different clinical implications.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results emphasize the importance of species-specific detection methods in understanding the epidemiology of adenoviral gastroenteritis and inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies in pediatric populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's findings are based on PCR results and should be interpreted cautiously due to the potential for incidental gastrointestinal passage or prolonged shedding of non-enteric adenoviruses, which may not reflect true causation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify the prevalence of human adenovirus species in stool samples from children with diarrhea in Najaf Governorate. Stool samples were collected between March and July 2025 and analyzed using multiplex PCR for adenovirus species A–F. Adenovirus species F was the most frequently detected (29%), followed by species C (15.9%), D (13.6%), E (11.3%), and B and A (6.8% each). Co-detection of species F and B was observed in 13.6% of samples. The results confirm the dominant role of species F in diarrheal disease and highlight the need for cautious interpretation of PCR results. These findings have implications for targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies in pediatric populations, but the study notes potential limitations due to the possibility of incidental passage or prolonged shedding of non-enteric adenoviruses.

title: A cross-sectional clinical and epidemiological overview of a cohort of acute infectious keratoconjunctivitis among war-displaced populations in Kassala State, Sudan, 2024.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Outbreaks of acute infectious conjunctivitis can spread rapidly in overcrowded communities and healthcare settings, highlighting the need for clinical and epidemiological data in war-displaced populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A facility- and camp-based cross-sectional study included 417 consecutive patients with acute conjunctivitis or keratoconjunctivitis who presented to ophthalmic services and internally displaced persons' settings in Kassala State, Sudan, from 15 August 2024 to 15 December 2024.
analysis.methods: Demographic, environmental, behavioural, clinical, treatment, and follow-up data were collected using a structured form, and descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, Mann-Whitney U tests, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and multivariable regression models were used as appropriate.
analysis.main_results: Among 417 patients, 231 (55.4%) were female, and 353 (84.7%) lived in urban areas; inadequate water/sanitation access was recorded in 125 (30.0%), a dusty environment in 224 (53.7%), a dirty environment in 317 (76.0%), a crowded environment in 223 (53.5%), and contact with a symptomatic person in 353 (84.7%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The clinical pattern is consistent with acute infectious keratoconjunctivitis, but the lack of laboratory testing prevents definitive classification as adenoviral epidemic keratoconjunctivitis or as enterovirus- or coxsackievirus-associated acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Future outbreak response in similar settings should include laboratory confirmation and viral typing, access to clean water, hand hygiene, separation of cases in eye-care services, and avoidance of shared personal items.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Diagnosis was clinical; laboratory viral typing was not performed, and all estimates are observational and are not interpreted as causal, indicating moderate evidence strength due to the lack of laboratory confirmation.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in Kassala State, Sudan, from August to December 2024, evaluated 417 patients with acute conjunctivitis or keratoconjunctivitis in war-displaced populations. The majority were female (55.4%) and urban residents (84.7%), with high rates of environmental risk factors like dirty (76.0%) and crowded (53.5%) conditions. Common symptoms included itching (94.2%) and redness (89.4%), while suspected bacterial superinfection (43.9%) and adenoviral keratoconjunctivitis (29.3%) were frequent clinical diagnoses. Recovery was associated with urban residence and lower symptom scores. The outbreak highlights the impact of displacement and limited healthcare access, with recommendations for laboratory confirmation and improved hygiene measures.

title: Helper-Dependent Adenoviral Vectors: Recent Advances and Emerging Applications.

analysis.scope_and_question: Helper-dependent adenoviral vectors (HDAdVs), which lack all viral coding sequences, enable the delivery of up to 35 kilobases (kb) of therapeutic DNA into target cells.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review provides a comprehensive, state-of-the-art overview of recent advances in the HDAdVs technology, summarizing key strategies for vector development, including capsid engineering and improvements in production methodologies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Despite the technical complexity of their production, HDAdVs have been extensively evaluated in numerous preclinical studies, and several clinical trials have recently been initiated. In conclusion, HDAdV-based vector systems hold considerable promise for the treatment of a wide range of diseases.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Nevertheless, several challenges must be addressed to enable broader clinical translation of HDAdVs. These include the complexity of large-scale manufacturing, achieving efficient and specific vector targeting, and overcoming host immune responses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Most preclinical applications have focused on targeting the liver and hematopoietic stem cells; however, additional organ systems and vaccination approaches based on HDAdVs are also being actively explored. In addition to preclinical progress, three recently initiated clinical trials using HDAdVs targeting knee osteoarthritis, chronic granulomatous disease, and solid tumors are highlighted.

analysis.summary_en: This review comprehensively examines helper-dependent adenoviral vectors (HDAdVs), which lack viral coding sequences and deliver up to 35 kb of therapeutic DNA. It highlights their large packaging capacity for complex transgenes, extensive preclinical evaluation, and recent clinical trials for conditions like knee osteoarthritis and solid tumors. Key strategies include capsid engineering and production improvements, with most preclinical focus on liver and hematopoietic stem cells. Challenges include large-scale manufacturing complexity, efficient targeting, and overcoming immune responses. The review concludes that HDAdVs hold significant promise for treating diverse diseases, with ongoing technological advancements enhancing their potential as versatile biotherapeutic tools.

title: Impact of Pre-Existing Adenovirus Immunity on Vaccine Immunity Induced by ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 in Immunodeficient Patients 2330644

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the impact of pre-existing immunity to human adenoviruses on immune responses to chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored COVID-19 vaccines, specifically ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, in immunodeficient patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed samples from healthcare workers and immunodeficient patients vaccinated with either nCoV-19 or BNT162b2.
analysis.methods: HuAd5 hexon-specific T cell responses were assessed using IFN-γ ELISpot and flow cytometry, while anti-HuAd5 antibodies were measured using Luminex for IgG and a GFP-expressing HuAd5 neutralization assay.
analysis.main_results: Significant T cell and antibody cross-reactivity between ChAdOx1 and HuAd5 was observed, with HuAd5-specific T cell frequencies positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 spike-specific T cell responses in nCoV-19 vaccinated immunodeficient individuals, but not in BNT162b2 recipients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings support a model in which heterologous pre-existing adenovirus-specific T cell immunity contributes to enhanced spike-specific T cell responses following adenovirus-vectored vaccination in antibody-deficient individuals, explaining higher T cell responses to adenovirus-vectored vaccines compared to mRNA vaccines in certain populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform vaccine design and immunization strategies for immunodeficient individuals, suggesting that pre-existing adenovirus immunity may modulate vaccine efficacy and potentially guide personalized vaccination approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate, as it includes both immunodeficient and healthcare worker cohorts but may have limitations in generalizability to broader populations or other adenovirus-vectored vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how pre-existing immunity to human adenovirus type 5 (HuAd5) affects immune responses to the chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored COVID-19 vaccine ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 in immunodeficient patients. The researchers found significant cross-reactivity between ChAdOx1 and HuAd5, with pre-existing HuAd5-specific T cells enhancing spike-specific T cell responses in nCoV-19 vaccinated individuals, an effect not seen with the mRNA vaccine BNT162b2. Conversely, higher anti-HuAd5 antibody levels were inversely correlated with spike-specific T cell responses. These findings suggest a bystander T cell effect that may explain why adenovirus-vectored vaccines often elicit stronger T cell responses than mRNA vaccines in immunodeficient or elderly populations, providing insights for optimizing vaccination strategies in these groups.

title: Efficacy, safety, and biodistribution of intranasally delivered adenoviral COVID-19 vaccine in hamsters

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed because COVID-19 continues to cause outbreaks worldwide despite extensive vaccination programs, and it aimed to develop better vaccines to protect vulnerable populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the efficacy, safety, persistence, and biodistribution of an adenovirus-based COVID-19 vaccine delivered intranasally in hamsters.
analysis.methods: The researchers conducted a comparative study of different adenoviral vectors, assessed longitudinal tissue analysis for transgene expression and vector DNA, and evaluated safety through biodistribution and clinical blood chemistry.
analysis.main_results: Ad5-S-3M induced a robust humoral immune response and effectively protected hamsters from SARS-CoV-2 infection; vaccine transgene expression and vector DNA persisted in nasal turbinates; and no significant changes in clinical blood chemistry were observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that mucosal delivery provides effective protection and that vector persistence may enhance immunity duration, extending knowledge of adenovector persistence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support intranasal delivery as a promising approach for mucosal vaccines against respiratory pathogens, potentially improving vaccine accessibility and durability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to animal models, but the controlled design and comprehensive assessment of efficacy, safety, and biodistribution provide moderate confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the efficacy, safety, and biodistribution of an intranasally delivered adenoviral COVID-19 vaccine in hamsters. The Ad5-S-3M vector induced a robust humoral immune response and effectively protected against SARS-CoV-2 infection, with durable transgene expression and vector DNA persistence in nasal tissues. Safety assessments showed no significant clinical or histological changes, supporting the vaccine's safety profile. The findings highlight intranasal delivery as a promising strategy for mucosal vaccines, potentially enhancing immunity duration and accessibility for respiratory pathogens.

title: A field-deployable immunofluorescence chip for adenovirus monitoring in groundwater systems

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rapid field detection of human adenoviruses in groundwater remains a critical technological gap, particularly for riverbank filtration systems exposed to extreme weather and contamination events.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we present the VIRUMEX chip, a field-deployable platform that captures and detects adenovirus proteins through immunofluorescence using antibody-functionalized 3D Sepharose beads integrated into a disposable flow-through microfluidic cartridge.
analysis.methods: Powered by a compact peristaltic pump, the system autonomously processes groundwater and yields fluorescence-based readouts in light intensity unit (LIU) within 4-8 h, enabling near-real time semi-quantitative pathogen surveillance.
analysis.main_results: Laboratory tests produced a clear detectable signal at 0.129 ng/mL (1000 LIU) for adenovirus hexon protein, and field deployment in the Erpe River catchment produced above-background fluorescence (800 LIU) in river water, providing proof-of-concept evidence with positive signal under real riverbank filtration conditions, while groundwater samples remained negative under the tested conditions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: By providing an on-site, rapid, and operationally simple detection method, the VIRUMEX chip provides an additional on-site virus screening prototype alongside qPCR and isothermal approaches and offers a promising prototype for integrating virus monitoring into groundwater safety frameworks which needs some further optimizations before it can be regarded as a fully validated detection tool.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The VIRUMEX chip enables near-real time semi-quantitative pathogen surveillance in groundwater systems, offering a promising prototype for integrating virus monitoring into groundwater safety frameworks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides proof-of-concept evidence with positive signal under real riverbank filtration conditions, but the VIRUMEX chip needs further optimizations before it can be regarded as a fully validated detection tool, indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the critical technological gap in rapid field detection of human adenoviruses in groundwater systems, particularly for riverbank filtration systems exposed to extreme weather and contamination events. The researchers developed the VIRUMEX chip, a field-deployable platform that captures and detects adenovirus proteins through immunofluorescence using antibody-functionalized 3D Sepharose beads integrated into a disposable flow-through microfluidic cartridge. The system autonomously processes groundwater and yields fluorescence-based readouts in light intensity units within 4-8 hours, enabling near-real time semi-quantitative pathogen surveillance. Laboratory tests showed a detectable signal at 0.129 ng/mL for adenovirus hexon protein, and field deployment in the Erpe River catchment produced above-background fluorescence in river water, though groundwater samples remained negative. The VIRUMEX chip offers a promising prototype for integrating virus monitoring into groundwater safety frameworks, though it requires further optimization before being fully validated.

title: Therapeutic potential of bovine type III interferon (IFN-γ3) as anti-bovine viral diarrhea virus agent 2305378

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate whether a replication-defective human adenovirus type 5 vector expressing bovine interferon lambda 3 (bovIFN-γ3) could reduce the severity of bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) infection and protect against thymus-associated lymphoid follicle depletion in calves.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A study was conducted using twenty-four colostrum-deprived calves divided into six groups, including uninoculated controls, BVDV-challenged controls, and groups treated with either an empty vector or the Ad5-bovIFN-γ3 vector via subcutaneous or intranasal administration.
analysis.methods: Calves received Ad5 vectors (∼7 × 10^10 PFU per animal) one day before and one day after BVDV challenge (∼6 × 10^7 TCID50 per animal), with nasal swabs and blood samples collected throughout the study and calves euthanized 14 days post-challenge.
analysis.main_results: Calves inoculated with BVDV experienced a transient decline in lymphocytes and monocytes, but real-time PCR showed no significant changes in BVDV shedding or viremia among groups; however, calves treated with Ad5-bovIFN-γ3 showed no BVDV-induced thymic weight reduction and greater protection of thymus-associated lymphoid follicles, particularly with subcutaneous administration.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that two doses of subcutaneous Ad5-bovIFN-γ3 can protect the thymus and prevent BVDV-induced thymic lymphoid depletion, though higher doses or multiple days of administration may be needed to fully prevent BVDV shedding and viremia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that Ad5-bovIFN-γ3 could be a potential therapeutic agent for mitigating BVDV-induced thymic damage in calves, with implications for developing interferon-based therapies for viral infections in livestock.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study did not demonstrate significant effects on BVDV shedding or viremia, and the sample size per group was small (n=3-6), limiting generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of a human adenovirus type 5 vector expressing bovine interferon lambda 3 (Ad5-bovIFN-γ3) against bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) in calves. Twenty-four colostrum-deprived calves were divided into six groups, including controls and those treated with Ad5-bovIFN-γ3 via subcutaneous or intranasal routes. While BVDV infection caused transient declines in lymphocytes and monocytes, Ad5-bovIFN-γ3 treatment prevented BVDV-induced thymic weight reduction and lymphoid follicle depletion, particularly with subcutaneous administration. However, no significant reduction in BVDV shedding or viremia was observed. The findings suggest Ad5-bovIFN-γ3 may protect thymic tissue but require higher doses or prolonged administration to fully control viral replication.
